summary: Complete the normal teardown of the real sent and deserialized stack objects already used by single-player director, gun-failure, ship-jam and kamikaze loopbacks. Copy payload/dispatch results first, then invoke the existing class-specific non-deleting destructor exactly once per object. Each body only stamps the root profile CE4974. No allocations, invented message inputs, duplicate bodies, payload frees or changes to delivery are introduced.

rows.reason: Missing producers/storage for screen+30h selection mode and the +C4h selection vector; existing UnitPickScreenState does not carry these inputs, so an empty vector/mode-zero projection would invent state.
Missing native party-brain array and planner+0Ch presence producer; the apparent stand-in is a stale difficulty comment, not an owned first-active-slot query.
Missing a native candidate-score-list producer carrying the sixteen score values/labels and candidate keys; the release host only owns command-target references, not that score list.
Missing the populated candidate-score-list object and selected candidate key required by the chosen-byte writer; wiring the release comment would operate on invented list state.
Missing the off-main-thread named-Lua-call producer and its actual argument queue; this host executes mission Lua on the main thread, so its current empty drain cannot supply deferred-call state.
Missing the ammo+48h flak-alternate record producer; the existing firepower adapter explicitly records that absence.

validation.called_total_explanation: The graph already counted these bodies through profile delete adapters before the patch; the new evidence is the fourteen direct calls on consumed real host message objects. Release ICF folds their identical code, so separate attribution uses the non-folding analysis build.
validation.boundary: Build and static executable call-site proof only. The game was not run; original FH3 exception unwinding and drop-in binary ABI are not claimed.

assumptions: The existing host intentionally owns both loopback objects on the stack. Non-deleting teardown is therefore the applicable part of the original queued object's scalar-delete path; scalar-delete flag 1 would incorrectly free host stack memory.
Only normal completion is changed. Existing native reconstruction bodies and profile lifetimes are reused without modification.
left: Other message families still omit normal teardown; continue only on already produced/consumed real objects. Pick-screen, native candidate-score-list, party-brain and deferred-Lua queue producers remain separate work.
